summary: The round 1 fixes are sound. The final pass in scripts/checks-template.sh records every check and then splits one 16 KB budget evenly among the failing ones, so the checker's result stays bounded however many checks fail, as the author decided for R1-13. `truncated` now reports both the line cut and the byte cut. The README contract, the setup order and the Gate stamp paragraph now match the code, and a gate-test case pins that adding a prose-only step leaves the hash unchanged. One low nit remains: inside a failing check's share, stdout can take bytes stderr does not use, but stderr cannot take bytes stdout does not use. This repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs. checks.sh writes only its own mktemp directory, so two runs at the same time cannot overlap on any data.

findings.title: A failing check's stderr never gets the share stdout leaves unused
findings.description: In emit_checks, a failing check's stderr allotment is min(share / 2, the bytes in its last 200 stderr lines), and stdout gets the rest (lines 126-131). The split only goes one way. An empty stderr gives stdout the whole share, but an empty or short stdout gives stderr nothing extra. So a lone failing check that reports on stderr (a `bash -n` syntax error, a `jq -e` failure, a tool that logs to stderr) keeps 8 KB of output while the other 8 KB of the budget goes unused. Before this change it kept 16 KB. Round 1's plan (Task 5) says "one failing check alone keeps today's 16 KB", which is true only when stdout fills its part. The README bullet at line 213 describes the asymmetry ("stderr takes at most half of a check's share"), so the code and the docs agree, but the bytes are given up for nothing. Traced by reading. The guard refuses to run scratch shell scripts for this role, so it was not executed.
findings.proposedFix: Make the split symmetric. Compute out_kept=$(tail -n "$keep" "$work/$name.out" | wc -c) beside err_kept. Set err_cap to min(err_kept, max(share / 2, share - out_kept)), then out_cap=$((share - err_cap)) as now. Each stream still gets at least half the share when both are long, the per-check total stays at most share, and a stream that is short or empty gives its unused bytes to the other. Change the README `truncated` bullet's parenthetical to "(each stream takes at least half of a check's share when both are long)" and the comment above the caps to match. The same lines go into .claude/redline/checks.sh with the rest of the R1-13 change the author is already carrying by hand.
